security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed expected local Playwright network access, filesystem artifact writes, and high-risk command execution in the server helper. Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the skill guidance should not discourage reviewing executable helper scripts before use.

remediation.issue: Server helper runs user-provided server commands through shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True where possible, or warn that only trusted project commands should be passed to --server.

remediation.issue: Server helper executes an arbitrary trailing command.
remediation.suggestion: Document the command execution boundary clearly and require users to inspect commands before running them.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions discourage reading helper source before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Replace this guidance with a short safety note that users may inspect helper code before running it.

remediation.issue: Examples write screenshots and logs to fixed local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Parameterize output paths or explain where artifacts are written before examples run.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Manual browser checks miss frontend regressions and console errors. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code automate local web app testing with Playwright.
actual_capabilities: Starts local development servers before running browser automation scripts.
Uses Playwright to navigate pages, click controls, and fill form fields.
Captures screenshots for visual inspection of rendered application state.
Collects browser console messages during automated test flows.
Discovers visible buttons, links, inputs, and selectors on rendered pages.
limitations: Requires Playwright and browser dependencies in the execution environment.
Focuses on local web applications, not hosted production monitoring.
Example scripts use fixed local URLs and output paths unless customized.
Generated automation still needs selectors and assertions matched to the application.

use_cases.title: Verify a Feature Before Commit
use_cases.description: Run a local app, exercise key UI paths, and confirm the page behaves as expected.

use_cases.title: Capture Debug Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect screenshots and console logs when a UI state is hard to inspect manually.

use_cases.title: Inspect an Unknown Interface
use_cases.description: Discover visible controls and selectors before writing a focused browser automation flow.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Local Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation of one running local page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app at http://localhost:5173. Take a screenshot and summarize visible problems.

prompt_templates.title: Find Usable Selectors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate discovery before writing a test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to inspect the rendered app. List visible buttons, links, inputs, and stable selectors for a login flow.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Feature Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task with server startup and interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the dev server with the helper script, run a Playwright flow for account creation, and capture screenshots after each major step.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Console Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Automate the failing UI path, collect console logs, identify JavaScript errors, and connect each error to likely source files.

output_examples.input: Test the dashboard page on my running local app.
output: Opened the local dashboard and waited for the network to become idle.
Captured a full-page screenshot for review.
Reported that the main chart loads, but the settings button is hidden at mobile width.

output_examples.input: Find the buttons and inputs on this rendered form.
output: Found three visible buttons, two text inputs, and one select control.
Suggested stable selectors based on labels, roles, and element identifiers.
Noted that one hidden input should not be used for user-facing automation.
Ran the checkout path in a headless browser.
Saved the relevant console messages to an output log.
Flagged one uncaught exception after payment method selection.

best_practices: Run helper scripts with the help flag before passing server commands.
Wait for stable page state before selecting elements or taking screenshots.
Keep generated Playwright scripts focused on one user flow at a time.
anti_patterns: Running untrusted server commands through the helper script.
Using fragile text selectors when roles or IDs are available.
Ignoring console errors because the visual page appears correct.

faq.question: Does this skill test deployed websites?
faq.answer: It is designed for local web applications, although Playwright can open any reachable URL.

faq.question: Does it require a running server?
faq.answer: A dynamic app needs a running server. The helper can start one or more local servers.

faq.question: Can it test static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to open local HTML files through file URLs.

faq.question: What artifacts can it create?
faq.answer: It can create screenshots and console log files when the automation script requests them.

faq.question: Is it safe to run any server command?
faq.answer: No. Server commands execute on the local machine and should come from trusted projects only.

faq.question: Does it write complete test suites automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples for focused browser automation scripts.
